1: Some professionals deliver successful projects. Others leave a lasting mark on the people, standards and industries around them. If that is you… keep watching.
2: Honorary Fellow of the Project Controls Institute… a board-conferred recognition of distinguished contribution, leadership and service. Your name — on the profession's public register.
3: NO examination. Separate from P-C-I's examined certifications. Every application is considered individually… and recognition is conferred solely at the Board's discretion.
4: If you have led teams, shaped standards, taught, published or governed — in project controls, cost engineering, finance, project management, or a closely related discipline — you may apply.
5: From infrastructure to energy, technology to aviation, project finance to government and academia. Wherever leadership shapes OUTCOMES… your contribution counts.
6: To be considered, you need at least eight years of relevant experience… including three at managerial level, and a demonstrable record of distinguished contribution. Meeting these criteria does not guarantee recognition.
7: There is NO fee. No nomination, assessment or credential charge. One application — your profile, résumé, career history and evidence — reviewed confidentially by the Board.
8: Those selected are recognised as an Honorary Fellow — recorded so anyone can verify it at source… and labelled honorary, never a passed examination. Accepted applicants may also receive access to the P-C-I student portal, study through Certuvo, and invitations to selected P-C-I A-I events, subject to programme terms.
9: Tell the Board whether your contribution aligns with project controls, project finance, or project management.
10: Your contribution has shaped the profession… Now let it be recognised. Apply today for the Board's consideration — at P-C-I-A-I dot org.
